long_biography.plain_text:
Vassilis Lamprou approaches hotel development as an architect as well as an owner. On Mykonos, he has led the design of a low-rise resort at Super Paradise Beach, while Lamprou Design & Constructions handles construction. The site is the group's first hotel venture outside northern Greece.

Mediterranean Hotels began assembling the land in 2018 before bringing the resort under Hilton's flagship brand through a franchise agreement. The Lamprou company retains ownership, while the franchise places the development within Hilton's international resort portfolio. Lamprou serves as the project's lead architect, extending the owner-designer role he established in the group's earlier resorts.

uncertainties.detail: The owner record contains only a name and broad Greek details, but all three saved social URLs explicitly bear Evangelia Xyptera's name. Institutional and independent sources identify Xyptera as Vassilis Lamprou's spouse, co-founder and fellow owner, while current project material names them separately. That unusual association, the hotel company bearing Lamprou's name and multiple exact-role sources resolve the hotelier with high confidence. The profiles remain wrong-person data and are flagged for manual removal rather than treated as his accounts.

Public results also include a Vasilis Lamprou with an aircraft-engineering career at Olympic Airways and Meton, and a younger Dr Vasileios Lamprou in cardiology in Manchester. Their sectors, employers, timelines and locations conflict with the Mediterranean Hotels founder. Other sparse exact-name profiles lacking the distinctive hotel-company evidence were not adopted.

Lamprou's co-founding, continuing ownership and development of Mediterranean Hotels provide affirmative evidence for broad Self-made. No reliable reviewed source establishes inheritance, a transfer of the principal hotel assets, or the financial and family platform available in 1996, so neither independent-start nor advantaged-start subtype is assigned.

Older sources call Lamprou president, chief executive, vice-president, owner and architect at different dates, while recent material identifies Xyptera as president and chief executive and Lamprou as developer and lead architect. The dossier therefore uses the durable co-founder, owner, developer and architect descriptions without assigning him a current executive title or a precise equity percentage.

Reliable sources use Vassilis, Vasilis and the formal company-name spelling Vasileios, but do not establish a middle name, preferred legal transliteration, birth date or birthplace. The saved Vassilis spelling is retained, with only whitespace normalized, and no unsupported personal-detail proposal is made.

Lamprou is identified as owner and architect of Mediterranean Village, as an architect-engineer in specialist hospitality reporting, and as lead architect of the current Mykonos project. That repeated, long-running practiced role satisfies the active Architect contract; no claim is made about architectural licensing, education or projects outside the hotel group.

Hotel operations represents the defining wealth and operating platform, while Architect captures a distinct substantial professional role. Luxury hospitality, resort operations, hotel investing, hospitality real estate and destination-resort development overlap the same evidence and are omitted under the minimum-useful-set rule. No taxonomy candidate was created.

Focused searches of LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok and personal websites did not establish an identity-secure personal account for Vassilis Lamprou. The official Mediterranean Hotels site is proposed as Company Website. The three Xyptera profiles are recorded only as manual correction candidates because proposed_socials cannot remove existing records.

The short biography presents the durable founder-operated hotel platform. The long profile independently develops Lamprou's architect-owner role and Mykonos expansion. Both omit the source-record vessel relationship, project budget, room counts and forecast opening dates so they remain accurate beyond a single development cycle.
